luds_pilgrim.text: Hush now. Six hundred years ago, folk crept down here to pray in secret, because their beliefs could get them burned.
Lollards, they were called: followers of John Wycliffe, who wanted the Bible in plain English for anyone to read. A dangerous idea, at the time.
The story goes that they were led by a Walter de Ludauk, the spelling varies, and that's how the chasm got its name. Whether that's true, the moss isn't telling.
Something green walks in here at dusk and in the fog. Holly in one hand, head in the other. If it offers you a game, don't take the first swing.
